note: Paper forms we can read off a photograph: the printed checkbox columns, in order, and which counted bucket each option feeds. Read by intake/js/paper.js. A sheet is read by geometry only — no OCR, no model, nothing leaving the phone — so a form can only be read if its option columns are declared here.
why: A CDCR-issued sign-in sheet is the only record of who was in the room, and it arrives as a photo. Retyping twelve rows of ticks into six questions is where counting errors come from.

forms.label: CDCR sign-in and demographic sheet
forms.note: Date, prepared by, service type and event across the top; one person per row; race, ethnicity, stable housing and veteran status per row. Screen sheets are printed by the institution, not by us, so there is no code to locate the page: the reader is calibrated by tapping the four corners of the table.
